title: chat.conversation_participants
description: Who is a party to these conversations. Batch: {"conversation_ids": [...]} -> {"conversations": {id: {"exists", "kind", "scope_key", "subject_type", "subject_key", "participants": [{"user_id", "role"}]}}}. An id that names no conversation — or is not a well-formed id at all — comes back as {"exists": false} rather than being omitted: the caller is holding that id for a reason and must be told it is dead, not left to infer it from an absence. This is the read a consumer previously avoided by storing its own copy of the two party ids on its own row, where it could silently go stale. Deliberately NOT a permission check: it answers who is a party, and whether that means the caller may do a thing is the caller's policy to apply.

conversation_ids.description: Conversation ids to answer for. Every id supplied appears in the answer.
